name: Asaiah
overview: Asaiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified as a Shilonite living in Jerusalem. His presence in the biblical record is brief, with no additional personal details or notes provided. He is noted specifically in 1 Chronicles 9:5.
namesAndTitles: The name Asaiah means "y-h-v-h has made," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's role in his existence. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:5 and does not carry any additional titles or meanings beyond this.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Asaiah as a descendant of Judah, linking him to the tribe of Judah. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Asaiah's significance lies in his identification as a Shilonite residing in Jerusalem, situating him within the restored community in Judah. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:5 contributes to the genealogical and communal record that highlights the continuity of God's people in the post-exilic period. Though not a prominent figure, Asaiah represents the faithful remnant within Judah, emphasizing God's ongoing work through His chosen tribe.
